That's really clear, thank you. Let me play back what I understood to make sure I've got the direction right:

> **The problem:** Your browser bookmarks have become a pile of links you rarely find again.
>
> **The goal:** A personal tool where the thing that matters most is *finding a saved link again quickly later*. To support that, you want to:
> - Save a link quickly, with its basic details filled in for you automatically
> - Organize with **tags** (not strict folders) — and **search** matters more than tidy organization
> - Mark whether something is still **to-read** vs. **finished**, without deleting it

Does that capture it? And is there anything you'd say is *the* single most important part — it sounds like **quick retrieval / search** is the heart of it, and the rest (auto-details, tags, to-read status) are means to make retrieval work. Is that the right emphasis?

One more thing so I set up the right kind of screens for you to react to: **what kind of app do you picture using this as?** For example a web app you open in a browser, a mobile app, a desktop app, or a terminal tool. (If you don't have a strong preference, just say so and I'll suggest one.)
